{{< include _poly-kit.qmd >}}

A **polyrhythm** is two or more rhythms played at the same time that divide the same span of time into
different numbers of even parts. In **3 against 2**, one part plays three even notes while another plays two,
and both start together. Each player on this page draws the cycle as a circle (the hand goes round once per
cycle) and as a grid (time runs left to right). Click a layer's name to mute it.

## 3 against 2

<div class="poly" data-layers="3;2" data-names="Three;Two" data-sounds="hi;lo" data-bpm="50"></div>

The two layers meet only on the first beat. In between, the notes fall at different places: the "two" lands
exactly between the second and third "three". A common way to say it is **"nice cup of tea"**:

Count six even pulses. The three falls on pulses 1, 3 and 5; the two on 1 and 4. Together they sound on
pulses 1, 3, 4 and 5, one syllable each: *nice* (both), *cup* (three), *of* (two), *tea* (three).

**Try it.** Tap the three with your right hand on your knee and the two with your left. Mute one layer
and play it yourself; then mute the other.

## The grid underneath: least common multiple

To write two even layers on one grid, you need a pulse that both fit into. That pulse count is the
**least common multiple** of the two numbers.

| Polyrhythm | Grid | Layer A hits on pulse | Layer B hits on pulse |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 : 2 | 6 | 1, 3, 5 | 1, 4 |
| 4 : 3 | 12 | 1, 4, 7, 10 | 1, 5, 9 |
| 5 : 4 | 20 | every 4th | every 5th |
| 5 : 3 | 15 | every 3rd | every 5th |

Below the player, the line under the grid shows the pulse count for whatever is playing.

## 4 against 3

<div class="poly" data-layers="3;4" data-names="Three (beat);Four" data-sounds="lo;hi" data-bpm="60" data-beat="0"></div>

A common saying for 4 against 3 is **"pass the golden butter"**, said evenly over twelve pulses.
Hear the three as the beat first (it is the lower sound), then switch: mute the three, feel the four as the beat,
and the three becomes the cross-rhythm.

## 5 against 4 and beyond

<div class="poly" data-layers="4;5" data-names="Four (beat);Five" data-sounds="lo;hi" data-bpm="60" data-beat="0"></div>

With bigger numbers no one counts the grid. Players hear the outer layer as a steady line that slides
against the beat and meets it again at the start of the cycle.

## Polyrhythm, polymeter and hemiola

These three words are often mixed up:

- **Polyrhythm**: different even divisions of the *same span* (3 notes and 2 notes in one bar).
- **Polymeter**: patterns of *different lengths* on the *same pulse* (a 5-step riff over 4-step bars). They
  drift apart and meet again after a while. The [math rock lesson](poly-math-rock.qmd) is about this.
- **Hemiola**: three groups of two heard against two groups of three, as in 6/8 heard as 3/4. It is
  3 against 2 at the level of beats.

<div class="poly" data-layers="X.x.x;X..." data-names="5-step riff;4-step bar" data-sounds="hi;kick" data-bpm="80" data-polymeter></div>

This one is polymeter: every step is the same length. Watch the 5-step pattern start in a different
place each bar until it lines up after 20 steps.
